title: Follow-ups from backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider's PR #368 review
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's PR #368 review of backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider (accepted -- that PR only records a genuine live-gateway research blocker as a `questions` entry and moves the task to `waiting_input`, no application code touched). Both items below are process/efficiency observations, not correctness bugs, and didn't block that PR's acceptance.

checklist.step:
PR #368 opened and pushed a branch/PR but never recorded a `git` block (branch/pr_number/pr_url/pushed_at) on backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider.json, unlike every other task-worker PR in this repo's history. `.claude/agents/task-worker.md` step 8 requires recording `git.*` when a PR is opened, but that instruction lives under the 'checklist complete, tests pass' completion path (step 8/9) -- step 6's separate 'hit a blocker, go to waiting_input' exit path doesn't explicitly say to record `git.*` even though it still results in an opened PR. Consider (a) backfilling the missing `git` block on backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider.json now that PR #368's number/URL/branch are known, and (b) clarifying task-worker.md step 6 to also require recording `git.*` whenever it does open a PR, for consistency with step 8.

Resolved: PR #369 (the follow-on resumption attempt) added a correct `git` block (branch/pr_number 369/pr_url/pushed_at) to backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider.json, per that PR's own review. Part (b), clarifying task-worker.md step 6 itself, is still open and not addressed by this.

Checklist items 2-4 on backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider.json (conid-caching decision, connection-check caching/degradation decision, and recording the DataProvider-protocol-reversal decision) are design judgment calls that don't actually depend on the live-gateway research blocker in item 1 -- they could have been decided and recorded in the same pass that raised the item-1 question, per CLAUDE.md's decision-memory convention (a worker decides and records what it can, rather than stalling everything on the one item that's genuinely blocked). Deferring all of them meant leaving decidable work on the table; when a human eventually answers the item-1 question and the task resumes, the next worker session will need to make these three decisions from scratch instead of picking them up already recorded. Not acted on for this review since it's a process/efficiency observation about how the blocker was raised, not a defect in what was recorded -- worth keeping in mind for whichever session resumes this task.

Resolved: once the live gateway was independently re-confirmed authenticated (pr-decision's override on PR #369), the resumed task-worker session decided and recorded checklist items 1-5 together in one pass, including items 2-4, rather than deferring any further -- see backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider.json's own `decisions` array.

Live-gateway research for backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider's checklist item 1 found that IBKRProvider.resolve_conid (its own existing ambiguity-degrades-to-None behavior, from backend-ibkr-symbol-resolution) cannot resolve 'AAPL' itself via a bare symbol search against a real gateway: /iserver/secdef/search returns FOUR distinct STK-sectioned conids for the exact symbol 'AAPL' (NASDAQ primary listing, a TSE-CDR listing, a Mexico-exchange listing, an EBS listing), which the existing ambiguity rule treats as unresolvable. This means the single most common example ticker in this codebase's own tests/docs can't actually be served by IBKR-primary mode today. Consider adding an exchange/listing-preference heuristic to _resolve_stk_conid (e.g. prefer a USD-denominated section, or the section matching a documented 'home exchange' convention) so common cross-listed US tickers resolve reliably rather than permanently falling back to 'no IBKR data for this ticker'. Not acted on in backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider itself per that task's own 'scope conservatively' guidance -- resolve_conid's ambiguity behavior is an existing, already-reviewed decision from a different task, and disambiguation logic is a non-trivial, separately-reviewable change.

Resolved: PR #369's review (pr-reviewer) escalated this from a deferred non-blocking nit to a BLOCKING finding on the main task itself (a real functional regression for the app's headline feature on its most common tickers, not an acceptable scope cut) -- the main task's resumed task-worker pass fixed `_resolve_stk_conid` directly (preferring the candidate whose search-result `description` names a primary US exchange -- NASDAQ/NYSE/AMEX/ARCA/BATS -- confirmed live against AAPL/MSFT/GOOGL/TSLA/NVDA/AMZN/IBM/KO/F/GE/SPY/QQQ and others), with new unit tests and docs/architecture/Backend.md §8 updated. See backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider.json's own `decisions` entry for the full live research.

While checking whether backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider's own docstring-only route change needed an openapi.json/frontend-types regeneration, found that backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts are ALREADY stale relative to each other on main, independent of this task: regenerating both (python scripts/export_openapi.py from backend/, then yarn generate:api-types from frontend/) pulled in several already-merged backend route docstring changes (GET /api/portfolio's swing-mode weekly-OHLCV prefetch note, GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis's concurrent daily/weekly/extended-data fetch note, IBKRScannerRunRequest's 'filter must be an array' note) that are present in backend/openapi.json but missing from the committed frontend/src/api/types.ts -- i.e. some prior PR(s) regenerated openapi.json without also regenerating (or committing) the frontend types, or vice versa. Worth a dedicated pass to regenerate frontend/src/api/types.ts properly (reviewing the resulting diff on its own, not bundled with an unrelated feature PR) and, if this keeps recurring, considering a CI check that fails when the two are out of sync.

pr-reviewer's PR #369 review (needs_work -- see backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider.json's `review.comments` for the blocking findings this was filed alongside) found a minor reuse/simplification issue while reviewing `app/api/dependencies.py`: `CachedDataProvider(YFinanceProvider(), StooqProvider(), db)` is constructed identically in two places -- `_build_live_data_provider`'s non-IBKR branch (the plain fallback path) and `_build_ibkr_primary_data_provider`'s `extended_data_provider` (the yfinance/Stooq carve-out chain used even while IBKR is primary). Worth factoring into a small shared helper (e.g. `_build_yfinance_stooq_provider(db)`) the next time either function is touched, so the two call sites can't silently drift apart. Non-blocking -- purely a duplication/readability nit, not a correctness issue.

Resolved: the main task's resumed task-worker pass (addressing PR #369's needs_work round, which touched both functions anyway) factored this into `_build_yfinance_stooq_provider(db)` and updated both call sites plus `_build_ibkr_primary_data_provider`'s own docstring to reference it.

pr-reviewer's PR #369 review (via a backgrounded code-review pass) found that `IBKRProvider`'s new `_gateway_status_cache`/`_conid_cache` instance dicts (app/data/ibkr_provider.py, backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider) are mutated with no lock, unlike the explicit `_ibkr_provider_singleton_lock` protecting the process-wide `IBKRProvider` singleton's own construction (app/api/dependencies.py). These caches are now hit far more heavily/concurrently than the pre-existing `_scanner_params_cache` ever was (every live-mode request's `_is_ibkr_connected()` check, plus every per-ticker OHLCV fetch fanned out via `ThreadPoolExecutor` in `enrich_positions_with_price`/day-trader-mode/`get_analysis`'s concurrent fetch). Worst case under a concurrent cold-cache race: two threads both see a miss for the same ticker/status check and both issue a duplicate live IBKR request, with whichever write lands last silently overwriting the other's cache entry -- wasted gateway round trips, not a wrong-answer correctness bug (the caches only ever store idempotent lookups), but worth a lock given how much more concurrent traffic this cache now sees than its one pre-existing sibling.

pr-reviewer's PR #369 review (via a backgrounded code-review pass) found that `get_data_provider_factory`'s own docstring (app/api/dependencies.py) still claims its live scope "wraps a fresh `CachedDataProvider`" per call, but `_live_scope` now calls `_build_live_data_provider(db)`, which returns an `IBKRPrimaryDataProvider` (not a `CachedDataProvider`) whenever IBKR is connected. Worth updating that docstring so a future reader doesn't assume IBKR-primary mode still has a yfinance/Stooq fallback at this call site, the same distinction `test_ohlcv_never_calls_yfinance_or_stooq_while_ibkr_connected_even_on_ibkr_failure` exists to pin down in test form.

Resolved: the main task's resumed task-worker pass updated `get_data_provider_factory`'s docstring to name `_build_live_data_provider` explicitly and call out that it's an `IBKRPrimaryDataProvider` (no yfinance/Stooq fallback) while IBKR is connected.

PR #369's round-2 review (via a backgrounded code-review pass on the cache-source-tagging fix commit) found that `CachedDataProvider._read_cache_for_current_source`'s docstring overstates what the fix actually guarantees: it claims a mode switch overwrites the other chain's cached rows in place "rather than leaving a second, duplicate set of rows behind", but that's only true for dates within the new source's own fetched range. IBKR's daily history is confirmed live to be ~999 bars (~4 calendar years, `IBKRProvider.get_daily_bars`'s own docstring) -- far shallower than yfinance's full decades-deep history -- so a ticker with years of pre-existing yfinance-sourced rows that then switches to IBKR-primary will have `_upsert` overwrite only the ~4-year overlapping window to `source="IBKRDataProvider"`; older yfinance rows outside that window are never revisited and stay permanently tagged with the stale source. Not a correctness bug (`_read_cache_for_current_source` still correctly filters them out as a miss, so they're never served as a false cache hit), but the table silently accumulates orphaned rows over repeated mode switches, and the docstring's "no duplicates left behind" claim is inaccurate for this case. Worth either correcting the docstring to document this as a known, accepted trade-off, or adding a cleanup pass (e.g. deleting other-source rows outside the new fetch's date range during `_upsert`).

PR #369's round-2 review (via a backgrounded code-review pass on the AAPL/conid-disambiguation fix commit) found that `_resolve_stk_conid` (app/data/ibkr_provider.py) builds its `candidates` dict keyed by conid (`dict[int, str | None]`), so if the same conid legitimately appears more than once in a `/iserver/secdef/search` response (the existing `test_duplicate_rows_for_the_same_conid_are_not_ambiguous` test documents this as a real shape -- "one row per derivative-bearing section returned as separate entries") with differing `description` values across those duplicate rows, the last occurrence in payload order silently wins with no validation that duplicate rows for one conid carry a consistent `description`. Not observed live (every live-tested ticker's duplicate-conid rows, where present, were not checked for description consistency across rows), but a speculative, payload-order-dependent robustness gap: a conid's primary-exchange-match outcome could flip depending on which duplicate row IBKR happens to return last. Worth either asserting/preferring a non-null `description` when duplicates disagree, or confirming live whether this can actually happen before spending effort hardening against it.
